status_effects.explanation: Her resort to heavy makeup and imitation of an actress to compete for her husband's attention casts her as anxious and artificial rather than composed and authentic.
Françoise's admiring account of his generosity toward Théodore locally elevates Legrandin's esteem.

He is staged as deeply valued by Gilberte and drawn into Saint-Loup's confidence, marking him as included and emotionally significant at Tansonville despite Saint-Loup's own growing coldness toward him.

appraisal_events.evidence: je fus stupéfait de la voir venir se mettre à table si étrangement différente de ce qu'elle était...comme si j'avais eu devant moi une actrice, une espèce de Théodora...je vis qu'elle était complètement peinte.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly registers Gilberte's drastic self-transformation - heavy makeup and imitation of the actress Rachel to compete for Saint-Loup's affection - as a startling, artificial disguise that diminishes her natural composure.

appraisal_events.evidence: ce Monsieur a tant de coeur...Il coucherait plutôt par terre et vous donnerait son lit. Il a trop aimé le petit Théodore pour le mettre dehors, bien sûr qu'il ne l'abandonnera jamais.
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise praises Legrandin (the unnamed patron of Théodore) as exceptionally generous and forgiving, granting him the 'beautiful role' of a devoted protector despite Théodore's tricks against him.

appraisal_events.evidence: ma venue avait été pour sa femme une joie telle qu'elle en était restée...transportée de joie tout un soir...je l'avais...miraculeusement sauvée du désespoir, «peut-être du pire».
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup reports that the narrator's arrival brought Gilberte great joy and relief from despair, staging the narrator as a valued and emotionally consequential presence in the household.
